method.scope: Consolidates both research reports in this conversation: cross-party military-policy comparisons, Savarkar’s programme, named service testimony, INA trials and the 1946 service unrest.
method.geography: Grouped chiefly by the place of an event or activity. Modern names aid navigation; historical provinces, cross-border Punjab and national/overseas material are labelled explicitly. A record can appear in more than one region without becoming a second claim.
method.verification: Statuses reflect what was inspected during the earlier research. An archive reference located through scholarship is not an inspected original. External links can move or require registration.
method.limits: Indexed searches included English and Marathi, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Gujarati, Punjabi, Malayalam and Urdu terms across the research. This is not an exhaustive survey of undigitised vernacular archives.
method.causation: Stated purpose, actual recruitment, individual motivation, later anti-colonial conduct and the causes of independence are separate propositions.
method.exclusions: The K. N. Rao letter is retained only as a sidelined research-trail entry, respecting the instruction to leave it aside. Unverified claims are documented as open questions, not adopted as fact.

records.title: Savarkar’s immediate programme
records.claim: The Madura programme sought Hindu entry into all three services, war-equipment skills, compulsory military education, Ram Sena organisation and qualified participation in civic guards.
records.limit: Its Hindu political objectives and restrictions on civic-guard use must remain part of comparisons.
records.locator: Madura address, PDF p. 93

records.title: Participation for national capacity
records.claim: Savarkar defended using Britain’s wartime manpower needs to acquire military and industrial capacity.
records.limit: Stated intention does not independently establish recruitment totals or later conduct.
records.locator: PDF pp. 86–88, especially p. 87
records.quote: with no intention of helping the British but of helping ourselves.

records.title: Training linked to eventual emancipation
records.claim: He urged modern military training and stronger Hindu representation, linking these with future freedom.
records.limit: He also required military discipline, subject to a Hindu-honour qualification; no operational mutiny order.
records.locator: PDF pp. 13–15; printed pp. 4–6
records.quote: political emancipation too of our motherland in the long run.

records.title: Recruitment-assistance boards
records.claim: The statement names a northern board under Ganpat Rai at Delhi and a southern board under Bhopatkar at Poona.
records.limit: Their applicant files would be valuable for tracing individual recruits.
records.locator: PDF p. 14

records.title: Ratnagiri recruiting tour
records.claim: Savarkar requested support for Phadke and Gogate’s district tour urging armed-service entry.
records.limit: Identifies recruiters, not a verified list of recruits.
records.locator: PDF p. 17

records.title: Capacity intended to outlast the war
records.claim: He reaffirmed militarisation despite rejecting the Cripps proposals.
records.limit: Anticipated national benefit is not evidence that his organisation caused subsequent revolts.
records.locator: PDF pp. 35–36; printed pp. 26–28
records.quote: an incalculable asset to the national strength even after the war.

records.title: Konkan naval recruitment appeal
records.claim: He urged naval recruiting assistance, particularly among Bhandari and Kharvi youth.
records.limit: An appeal does not establish individual enlistment motives.
records.locator: PDF pp. 37–38

records.title: Retrospective credit to armed struggle
records.claim: His Republic message credited multiple streams, including the INA and military rebellion.
records.limit: Post-independence interpretation, not a wartime forecast.
records.locator: PDF pp. 155–156; printed pp. 141–142

records.title: P. C. Joshi: enlist without awaiting national government
records.claim: Joshi explicitly advocated recruiting into the existing fighting forces and rejected postponement until a National Indian Army existed. He also proposed armed Home Guards, citizen training and industrial equipment.
records.limit: Official communist policy within the anti-fascist people’s war; not endorsement of Savarkar’s Hindu programme.
records.locator: Printed pp. 22–23, Home Guards and Recruitment
records.quote: We want to see the recruitment to the fighting forces thousand-fold.
records.place: Pamphlet published in London; all-India programme

records.title: K. M. Ashraf formally adopts the communist defence
records.claim: Ashraf submitted Joshi’s defence of party policy on behalf of communist members of the AICC.
records.limit: Organisational action, not merely a set of personal opinions; no endorsement of Savarkar established.
records.locator: Letter to Kripalani, Bombay

records.title: Congress charges against communist wartime activity
records.claim: The charge sheet alleged sustained communist propaganda for the war effort from June 1942.
records.limit: An adversarial allegation; read alongside Ashraf and Joshi’s response.
records.locator: Charge sheet addressed to Sardesai

records.title: Ambedkar: Mahar recruitment and removal of exclusion
records.claim: Ambedkar’s newspaper letter describes his intervention with the Bombay Governor over Mahar exclusion, welcomes a battalion, urges enlistment and seeks continued postwar employment.
records.limit: An independent recruitment and equality programme; Ambedkar was neither a Congress nor CPI spokesman.
records.locator: Writings and Speeches 17/I, pp. 306–307
records.quote: I appeal to the Mahars to take advantage of this opportunity

records.title: Nehru: citizen army and small-arms manufacture
records.claim: Nehru proposed a citizen army or militia, much greater factory output and conversion of non-essential production to small arms.
records.limit: His national-government conditions are integral; this does not establish support for colonial recruitment on Savarkar’s terms.
records.locator: Selected Works, first series, vol. 12, pp. 213–227
records.quote: Our conception was one of developing a citizen army or militia.

records.title: Nehru at Lucknow: arms linked with freedom
records.claim: He argued that India required both freedom and arms, and that Britain should arm Indians for effective defence.
records.limit: Conditional national defence, not an authenticated endorsement of Savarkar’s scheme.
records.locator: Selected Works 12, pp. 333–338

records.title: Nehru: a people’s army and industrialisation
records.claim: His Allahabad speech proposed armed as well as nonviolent resistance to Japan.
records.limit: Preserve the political context shortly before Quit India.
records.locator: Selected Works 12, pp. 426–427
records.quote: By raising a people’s army. By increasing production and industrialisation.

records.title: Azad: negotiated military cooperation
records.claim: Azad’s letter, drafted by Nehru, accepted continued operational command, existing military organisation and London’s higher strategy with Indian representation, alongside a national government organising popular defence.
records.limit: A Congress negotiating position contingent on political responsibility.
records.locator: Selected Works 12, pp. 202–208; Transfer of Power I, pp. 726–730

records.title: Rajaji supports military education personally
records.claim: In the Madras militia discussion, Rajaji supported military education and national defence facilities as a personal view.
records.limit: He sought withdrawal of the particular resolution, opposing provincial fragmentation and favouring a united Indian organisation.
records.locator: Selected Works VI, pp. 209–212, item 140; The Hindu, 29 September 1937

records.title: Rajaji’s wartime national-army proposal

records.title: Khare’s school and college rifle clubs
records.claim: Khare told the Lok Sabha that, as Congress premier of the Central Provinces and Berar, he permitted rifle clubs in schools and colleges.
records.limit: His own retrospective testimony; later Mahasabha activity must not be labelled Congress action. Historical province also extended beyond these modern states.
records.locator: Lok Sabha, 5 March 1954, cols. 1335–1336; PDF p. 9
records.quote: permit freely the starting of rifle clubs in all the schools and colleges there.

records.title: Savarkar congratulates Khare over rifle training

records.title: Gandhi at Nadiad: wartime service and future strength

records.limit: First World War precedent; not support for Savarkar’s later programme.
records.locator: CWMG original vol. 14, pp. 435–439, especially p. 438
records.quote: With that strength, we may even fight the Empire, should it play foul with us.

records.title: Gandhi and Patel organise actual recruitment

records.limit: Demonstrates recruitment action in 1918, not Patel’s endorsement of the WWII Savarkar scheme.

records.title: Roy’s conference links anti-fascism with future freedom
records.claim: A contemporary newsreel records Roy presiding at the RDP conference in Lucknow, with a banner connecting today’s anti-fascist fight to tomorrow’s Indian freedom.
records.limit: The quotation is a conference banner, not necessarily Roy’s spoken words. Government-sponsored film; Roy was an RDP leader, not a CPI spokesman.
records.locator: Indian Movietone News No. 9, INR 9
records.quote: The same arm that fights Fascism today SHALL free India tomorrow

records.title: Savarkar’s Kanpur appeal in the same newsreel

records.limit: Juxtaposition in a newsreel does not establish cooperation between Roy and Savarkar.
records.locator: Indian Movietone News No. 9, INR 9

records.title: Faiz Ahmed Faiz’s wartime army service
records.claim: The official honours record lists Faiz as Captain, temporary Major, Indian Army. He later acknowledged joining in an interview with I. A. Rehman.
records.limit: Shows personal service by a Marxist intellectual, not a Savarkar-inspired enlistment or his own recruiting campaign. Punjab here is a historical association, not a modern Indian-state service location.
records.locator: London Gazette supplement 36866, p. 14; Herald, March 1984

records.title: R. P. Paranjpe and Poona rifle clubs
